---
title: "Course files and datasets"
---

All datasets are simulated teaching examples. Downloading a file is the start
of the workflow: find it, extract it if needed, and place it where you can return
to it. Read the [project setup guide](../intro/r-rstudio.qmd) for step-by-step help.

| Download | Used for | What it contains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [course-files.zip](course-files.zip) | R practicals, weeks 2–5 | An RStudio project, all datasets and dictionaries, a working `report.Rmd`, and output folders |
| [lab-data.zip](lab-data.zip) | Command line, week 1 | A README, a sample manifest, four small measurement files, and field notes |
| [organic-lab.zip](organic-lab.zip) | Alternative command-line practice | Supplied organic sample labels, a product-recovery table, README, and dictionary; no prior chemistry needed |
| [Starter R Markdown](../report.Rmd) | Inspect or replace the template | The same working first report supplied in the project ZIP |
| [Data dictionary](../data/README.md) | Understand the biological design | Units, identifiers, missing values, and independent experimental units |

Keep the extracted `introcomputing-course` folder together. All `.Rmd` reports
should be saved in its root, beside `introcomputing.Rproj`, so paths such as
`data/seedlings.csv` mean the same thing throughout the course.

The shell practice archive is separate. On Windows, the Ubuntu home folder and
your normal Windows Documents folder are different locations. A remote computer
is another location again. Practise transferring one small file deliberately;
do not assume these copies synchronise.

The course project also includes `data/organic-recovery.csv`, for short organic
laboratory transfer exercises. It supplies the maximum possible and collected
product masses, with the calculation defined in each exercise. Choose a transfer
option where a lesson offers it; you do not need to complete every context or
have taken another chemistry course.
